nodes.label: Local-First Principle
nodes.rationale: Local-first is non-negotiable: the device owns the data; cloud is an optional encrypted replica, never the source of truth.

nodes.label: Local-First Architecture
nodes.rationale: Personal financial records belong solely to the user; unlike conventional cloud fintech platforms that harvest and profile bank accounts, MyFinanceOS is built entirely on a Local-First Architecture with no centralized backend databases.

nodes.label: Zero Server Storage Guarantee
nodes.rationale: No centralized backend databases store, inspect, process, or sell account balances, salary slips, investment portfolios, tax records, or transaction logs.

nodes.label: On-Device Computing
nodes.rationale: All calculations (Net Worth rollups, XIRR returns, Old vs New tax slabs, Sankey money flow graphs, EMI schedules) execute locally inside the client runtime.

nodes.label: Client-Side Encryption & Zero-Knowledge Storage
nodes.rationale: Enables multi-device synchronisation without exposing users to centralized cloud data breach vectors; the decryption key is derived from the user PIN and never leaves the device, so the vendor physically cannot view, index, read, or sell financial data.

nodes.label: Software License & Scope of Use

nodes.label: Unencumbered User Data Ownership
nodes.rationale: User retains 100% ownership over financial records; zero vendor lock-in via free JSON/CSV backups; no commercial harvesting or claims over user data.

nodes.label: RTK - Rust Token Killer CLI Proxy Rule
nodes.rationale: RTK filters and compresses command output before it reaches the LLM context, cutting up to 90% of the bash output on common operations; always prefix shell commands with rtk instead of raw commands.

nodes.rationale: Core Philosophy: data lives on the user's machine first; when opted in, it syncs end-to-end-encrypted to Supabase so the dashboard follows across devices, with Google OAuth handling identity while the encrypted payload stays unreadable to any third party, including the maker.

nodes.label: Security & Privacy Model / Encryption Flow
nodes.rationale: PIN is never stored (derived key exists only in RAM during session), no plaintext ever leaves the browser, AES-GCM authentication tags provide tamper detection, fresh salt+IV per operation gives forward secrecy, and 100,000 PBKDF2 iterations plus Argon2id resist brute-force attacks.

nodes.rationale: Designs that only work with perfect data aren't production-ready; budget 30-40% text expansion, use logical properties for RTL, use Intl for date/number formatting, and never trust client-side validation alone.

nodes.label: Squint Test
nodes.rationale: With detail blurred, can you still identify the primary element, the secondary element, and the major groups in order; a reading-order check that precedes moving any boxes.

nodes.label: Spatial Thesis
nodes.rationale: Name the primary reading or task path, what belongs together and what must separate, which element leads, and the intended density and rhythm before editing; choose the simplest structural model that expresses those relationships.

nodes.label: CSP Detection and Consent
nodes.rationale: The CSP patch is guarded by NODE_ENV === development so the http://localhost:8400 allowance only appears in dev and never reaches production; asked once per project and recorded as cspChecked.

nodes.label: Framework Injection Adapters
nodes.rationale: SvelteKit, Nuxt, and TanStack Start server-render their document shell, so a raw script in the entry template will not execute reliably; each gets a dedicated dev-only injection adapter detected at inject time.

nodes.label: Identity Lock
nodes.rationale: Live runs on an existing surface; the brand is already chosen. The job is variation within identity, and absence of DESIGN.md is never an excuse to depart - identity is extracted from CSS variables, computed styles, and sibling components.

nodes.label: Parameter Contract
nodes.rationale: 0-4 coarse knobs per variant, budget scaled to the element's visual weight; knobs drive CSS variables or data attributes so the browser docks one control per parameter with zero regeneration cost.

nodes.label: Carbonize Cleanup
nodes.rationale: The accepted variant is stitched into source with markers and inline CSS so the browser renders with no gap; rewriting it into permanent form before anything else prevents dead @scope rules, wrapper divs, and marker comments accumulating across sessions.

nodes.label: The Product Slop Test
nodes.rationale: Product UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose; the bar is earned familiarity and the tool should disappear into the task.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals
nodes.rationale: Performance is a feature: identify the actual bottleneck for this interface, fix it, then measure. LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1.

nodes.label: Context-Aware Menu
nodes.rationale: When /impeccable is invoked with no argument, lead with 2-3 highest-value next commands backed by context signals instead of a static menu; the recommendation is a suggestion the user confirms, never auto-run.

nodes.label: Discovery Interview
nodes.rationale: Do not dump a questionnaire or repeat settled facts; ask 2-3 high-leverage questions per round and assert likely readings, inviting correction, because sparse prompts need an answer round while precise prompts need only compact confirmation.
